neighbours.label: 'when' introducing the event that triggers a reaction or turn in a narrative or news report (grew worried when, but when she refuses), as against 'when' in questions and instructions
fire: Residents grew alarmed when smoke appeared over the ridge.
The plan falls apart when her partner betrays the crew.
Markets panicked when the bank announced heavy losses.
Sam is delighted when a stranger offers him a job in the city.
The villagers were stunned when the old mill burned down.
Everything changes when a mysterious girl moves in next door.
Fans were furious when the club sold its star striker.
But when the storm cuts the power, the guests turn on each other.
quiet: Do you know when the smoke alarm was last tested?
Please lock the door when you leave the office.
When does the bank open on Saturdays?
Text me when the stranger at the desk calls your name.
Turn off the oven when the timer rings.
Ask the landlord when the new tenant moves in next door.
Remind me when the club meeting starts tomorrow.
Unplug the heater when the storm cuts the power.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.8 on ' when' in narrative event clauses; question and instruction 'when' 0.0-0.1
notes: Card peaks ' when' x7, ' When' x2, in plot synopses and history. Probe: 'Officials grew worried when the river rose' 0.830; 'But when she refuses' 0.754 (peak ' refuses'); 'turns dark when his brother disappears' 0.590; 'thrilled when a letter arrives' 0.254; 'When is the next train' 0.037; 'Call me when you get home' 0.014; but 'turns dark after his brother disappears' 0.623 (plot clause without 'when' also fires). Near misses here use non-narrative 'when', not plot clauses with other conjunctions.
